name: Logics-SWE-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: GQA plus gated linear attention: 30 of 40 layers are linear_attention and 10 are full_attention, one every fourth layer
notes:
ADDED 2026-10-30 from the trending sweep, step 4b (derivative pass on a catalog base). A category-aware multi-teacher on-policy-distillation (MOPD) fine-tune of Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, not a new base: architecture fields are inherited unchanged from models/qwen3-6-35b-a3b (gated-linear-attention hybrid, 256 routed experts, 8 per token + shared expert, 10 of 40 layers full attention). Paper arXiv:2609.23377, code github.com/alibaba/AgenticBigBang.

PARAMS: HF safetensors total 35,107,181,936 = 35.107B, which is BELOW the base record's 35.952B. The card gives no parameter breakdown, so the 0.85B gap is UNEXPLAINED here - candidates are a dropped vision tower or a different counting convention on the base; it is not a depth change (num_layers 40 matches the base). Recorded as printed by the safetensors index, not adjusted to the base.

HARDWARE GATE: passes. active_params_b 3.0 (inherited from the base, MoE) <= 40, and 35.107 x 0.5 GiB = ~17.6 GiB at 4-bit <= 128 GiB. This is the MoE-stays-fast-with-experts-in-RAM shape the catalog prefers: 3B active per token, so a low-VRAM box keeps 3B of weights hot and streams experts.

EVIDENCE CAVEAT: every row is the card's own table with the base column printed beside it, so it is a same-card comparison. The card does NOT name the agent scaffold or harness per row (only 'the full model-and-agent evaluation setups'), and the numbers are three-round means. It WINS on all five printed rows and LOSES on nothing printed - but a card that prints only wins has no row to lose. SWE-bench Pro V2 Hard-51 is a subset of SWE-bench Pro V2, not an independent test.
